Es ist am Anfang nicht einfach, vom sehr einfachen Wunderlist auf ToDoist umzusteigen, aber ich gewöhne mich langsam und möchte einige Features nicht mehr missen. Für Projektmanagement gibt es wohl nichts besseres in der Form. Der Preis ist natürlich nicht ohne, aufgrund der häufigen Benutzung und des wirklich guten Dienstes bin ich dennoch bereit, diesen zu zahlen.

text: Ich nutze Todoist (Premium) jetzt seit ungefähr einem Jahr auf dem PC (Win7) , Laptop und Tablet (Windows10) und dem Handy (Android 8) Einer der Gründe mich für Todoist zu entscheiden, war die Anbindung an Alexa, die auch super klappt.  Ich habe ADHS und "benötige" aus diesem Grund ein verlässliches Task-Management. Bisher klappte das auch einwandfrei. Die Synchronisation zwischen den Geräten lief problemlos, regelmässige Updates, Teamfähig,ein wirklich schneller und kompetenter Support, annehmbarer Preis. Vor ca einer Woche bemerkte ich, dass plötzlich Aufgaben fehlten. Definitiv nicht von mir gelöscht, waren sie ins Nirvana verschwunden. Erst nur eine Handvoll und letztlich müssen es an die 40 Tasks gewesen sein, die einfach verschwunden waren. Der Support war zwar anfangs sehr bemüht, hat aber letztlich auch keine Lösung gefunden. Ein Zustand, der nicht tragbar ist, wenn man sich auf die App verlassen "muss". Somit blieb nur eines: Alle Aufgaben in ein anderes, ähnliches Produkt übertragen und Todoist den Rücken kehren. Schade um die verbleibenden Premium-Monate...
author: Ein Google-Nutzer
developer_reply: Wir können Sie versichern, dass user Support definitiv eine Lösung für das Problem finden wird.

Dank und auch Kompliment für die gute übersichtliche Gestaltung. 😀👍 Einen 
Kritikpunkt der auch einzig und allein für den Stern Abzug sorgt habe ich 
dann aber doch. Ich habe viele ToDos die täglich oder wöchentlich anfallen 
und sehe leider noch keine Option wiederkehrende ToDos automatisch 
einzustellen 🤔 vielleicht finde ich es einfach nicht oder brauche Premium 
dazu aber wenn ihr mir das noch ermöglicht gibt's auch 5 Sterne 😄👍 
Update: die Entwickler haben mir eine mir bis dato unbekannte Lösung 
aufgezeigt. Klappt super daher jetzt auch 5 Sterne TOP !

developer_reply: Sebastian, vielen Dank für Ihr Feedback. Sie können wiederkehrende Aufgaben erstellen indem Sie einfach nur z.B. "jeden Tag" oder "alle 2 Wochen", "jeden Montag um 16 Uhr" usw. im Namen der Aufgabe eintippen :) Mehr Infos dazu finden Sie auf https://support.todoist.com/hc/de/articles/360000636289-Ein-wiederkehrendes-F%C3%A4lligkeitsdatum-festlegen-

text:
Das ist so ziemlich die motivierendste App die ich am Handy habe. Ich 
benutze diese App seit Anfang des Schuljahres eigendlich so nebenbei, nur 
nach und nach habe ich begriffen, dass diese App in stressigen Phasen (wie 
zurzeit) mir beim Denken hilft und mich motiviert dass ich weitermache. Sie 
übernimmt mir den Tag zu sortieren, meine Gedanken, als auch meine 
Packlisten. Mit einprägsamen Kürzeln kann man schnell den Tag und die 
Priorität bestimmen. Und los gehts. Sie ist ideal für die Leute, die sich 
in sehr Leistungsdruck-intensiven Situationen wiederfinden, als auch für 
die, die ihren Tag so produktiv wie möglich gestalten wollen. Beides trifft 
voll und ganz auf mich zu, was Todoist zu meinem Begleiter #1 machte. Und 
bevor ihr skeptisch werdet, wie man nur so positiv über eine App schreiben 
kann: Ich bekomme nichts bezahlt und habe auch keinen Premiumaccount 
(schade dass man dazuzahlen muss) Jedoch würde ich nichts gegen eine 
kostenlose Geschmacksprobe sagen *zwinker*.

text:
Erfüllt fast alle meine Bedürfnisse nach einer modernen todo App. Nachteile 
sind aus meiner Sicht: 1. Einen einfachen Eintrag zu machen ist zu 
umständlich. 2. Entwickler sitzt in einem Staat dessen Politik 
unvorhersehbar und chaotisch ist (USA). Man kann nie wissen ob morgen 
Nutzungsverbote für unliebsame Staaten (Europa) erlassen oder Zusatzzölle 
erhoben werden. 3. VOR ALLEM aber kann man seinen SYNC Server nicht selbst 
wählen und ist damit den Datennutzungs-bestimmungen eines fremden Staates 
ausgeliefert der sich (siehe Snowden Affäre und siehe 2.) als nicht 
userfreundlich erwiesen hat.

text: Die App ist recht teuer, weil man die Nutzung monatlich bezahlen muss. - Am schlimmsten aber ist die Integration mit dem Google Kalender. Das neue Synchronisationmodul hat bei mir alle Kalendereinträge gelöscht. Mag sein, dass dabei ein Handlingfehler von mir eine Rolle gespielt hat, aber bei einem serienreifen Produkt ohne Betastatus usw. sollte das einem nicht unerfahrenen Benutzer wie mir nicht passieren können. Da müsste es zahlreiche Warnungen vor fatalen Fehlern und Backup-Möglichkeiten geben. - Ich bin sehr enttäuscht!  Konkret habe ich die synchronisierten Aufgaben in Todoist weiterbearbeitet, indem ich sie in Unteraufgaben gegliedert habe. Dadurch verschwanden sie im Kalender. Beim Zurückkopieren waren zunächst alle Endzeiten verloren (Korrekturzeitraum vom 20.1. bis 20.2., statt dessen nur noch ein Tag).  Als ich das mühsam wieder eingepflegt habe, sind alle Termine durch irgendeinen weiteren Fehler verschwunden. So etwas darf nicht passieren! Der Kalender ist für mich kein Spielzeug.
author: Ein Google-Nutzer
developer_reply: Tilman, wir arbeiten schon an allen Problemen mit der Kalender Integration und hoffen, dass alles bald 100% Fehlerfrei funktionieren wird.

text: War auf meinem neuen Huawei vorinstalliert. Also wollte ich es doch mal ein Jahr als kostenloses Premium versuchen und ausprobieren. Was nützt mir eine morgendliche Mail, in der alle Termine des Tages aufgelistet sind. Eine Erinnerung an von mir vorgegebenen Zeitpunkten ist eigentlich Standart. Hier wohl nicht. Einzig die einfache Eingabe von sich wiederholenden Terminen finde ich wirklich gut, und nur deshalb gebe ich zwei Sterne.  Trotzdem werde ich die App wieder deaktivieren. Löschen lässt sie sich ja leider nicht von meinem Huawei-Mobiltelefon.
author: Ein Google-Nutzer
developer_reply: Setzen Sie sich bitte mit support@todoist.com in Verbindung und wir werden Ihr Premium Konto aktivieren. Es tut uns leid, dass Sie die morgendsliche Mail als nutzlos befinden, Sie können sie jederzeit in den Einstellungen ausschalten. Mit Todoist Premium können Sie Erinnerungen für jeden beliebigen Zeitpunkt einstellen können.

Mir fehlen lediglich zwei Funktionen: zum einen möchte ich Start- und Endzeitpunkte so eintragen können, dass sich bei Änderung des einen Punktes und definierter Dauer auch der andere Punkt automatisch anpasst und  ein laufendes Projekt jeden Tag als ToDo zu sehen ist. Auf Nachfrage wann oder wie ich eine Rechnung erhalte: “Unfortunately, we're not issuing invoices yet, but we'll offer such service in the future.” Wer die Premium Features nicht nutzen möchte, kann viele andere ToDo App's nutzen ohne einen Account anlegen zu müssen.

developer_reply: Simon, wir erstellen immer Rechnungen per Anfrage, wenn Sie über unsere Seite oder PayPal bezahlt haben. Wenn Sie Todoist Premium durch Google oder Apple gekauft haben, dann darf nur Google oder Apple (der Verkäufer) Ihnen eine Rechnung erstellen da kein Verkauf zwischen Ihnen und uns sondern Ihnen und Google/Apple statt gefunden hat.

text: Wo liegt der Unterschied zwischen "Posteingang" , "Projekt" und "Erledigung" ? Und wie kann ich eine Aufgabe (zb. Einkaufsliste) teilen?
author: Ein Google-Nutzer
developer_reply: Mike, der Posteingang ist ein Projekt und Projekte sind wie Ordner, in denen Sie Ihre Aufgaben speichern. Wenn Sie eine Aufgabe erledigen, dann können Sie sie als "erledigt" markieren, als ob Sie sie auf einer Liste durchstreichen würden. Sie können auch Unteraufgaben benutzen z.B. die Aufgabe "Einkaufsliste" kann mehrere Unteraufgaben haben.

I could not find any cases of others having this issue online, so maybe I'm just a moron. And morons leave 2-star reviews for things that are their own fault.
author: Juliet Salinas
developer_reply: Hi Juliet, in Todoist, recurring tasks are based on completions. This means that a task will only appear on its due date once the previous instance has been completed. If you create a task that repeats daily, it will only show up in the "Upcoming" view on the current day. Once you complete the task, it will then appear on the following day.

text: TODoist is a FANTASTIC app! It is one of the better apps that I have worked with in business, yet to be honest I first stumbled upon it by looking for a timer app that would interact / syncronize with Trello. It was then that I read that ToDoist DOES sync with many other apps, and that if I were using Pomodone (a pomodoro timer app), then all that I do in ToDoist would be readily synced into Pomodone, allowing me to not only schedule and prioritize my time but ALSO to discipline myself to accomplish it through timers. If you are using ToDoist than Pomodone seems like it was built purely to enable your productivity goals in ToDoist! Together, these apps are unbeatable! Having said all of this, ToDoist is alone ABSOLUTELY worth the time and money to learn and to purchase! I have used MANY different scheduling or GTD systems, and ToDoist is far and away the best that I have used! Do yourself a great favor and learn the keyboard shortcuts!! These are very powerful in action. The app’s ability to understand common language / phrasing is simply uncanny! REALLY WELL DONE!!! I highly recommend ToDoist. I mysefl committed to changing the system that I was already using, (largely because of the tie-in between ToDoist and Trello and Pomodone), and I can certify that it was WELL worth my investment of time!

Adding a task at the bottom of the list means the new thing is lost from view and I have to manually rearrange the list. On the web app, you can control where to add a new item by using Shift+A, but there is no preference to ALWAYS do this! Also, sorting by date either doesn't work, or sorts the wrong way, because the newest tasks are still at the bottom. I cannot believe that this is the default, behavior, and that it cannot be set in a USER PREFERENCE. I sooooo miss Wunderlist.

I can schedule my reading task daily, but if I complete the task at 12 AM on the night of November 1st, it counts as "tomorrow" and won't automatically reappear until November 3rd. I propose that Todoist have a night-owl setting, in which we late-nighters can define when our days end. I don't want my reading to count for November 2 if I'm completing the task for November 1 before I've gone to sleep. I don't want Todoist to skip that task to November 3 even if it is the next calendar day because I won't have done my reading for November 2. I wish that we would be able to define our 24 hour period as one day instead of solely relying on Calendar dates.

text: Very nice app to organise.
author: A Google user

text:
In project view I cannot hide completed tasks and my projects stay 
cluttered with completed tasks. I really want to like this app and have it 
become my primary tool for getting things done but this is a huge flaw for 
my use. If you think about a physical pen and paper todo list, there's 
something satisfying about crossing a line through the item or checking a 
once-blank box, that isn't there in this app. I want to feel like I can 
clearly see what I have left to do for the day. I would really appreciate 
if completing tasks made the task significantly different (strikethrough or 
making the text of completed tasks more transparent). I want to see that 
I've completed something (for the day). I think another fun addition for 
the programmers would be visually rewarding recurring tasks being completed 
with a little fireworks display or a little cute puppy or something next to 
the task. Please consider these additions to the app as it would really 
improve my life. I will still use this app but I would love for the app to 
respond more to my little successes each day. Thank you!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Tyler, you can split big tasks into sub-tasks and when you complete them, they will indeed stay on the list, grayed-out until you complete their parent. We'll look into adding more rewarding effects in the future :)

text: Great app to remind me to do things
author: A Google user

text:
Highly recommend for anyone who has tasks to complete. No one tool is 
perfect, but this comes really darn close, and few times have there been 
things that aren't possible in my system. I picked up this app while 
learning the GTD system, and it has seriously improved my happiness and 
stress. I now see tasks and actionable things that I can do instead of a 
dread of vauge projects. If you are going to be serious, premium is well 
worth it. Personally, I have a @waiting and @next_action tags as well as 
several location ones that help me look at exactly what the work I can do 
right now is. Comments are suprisingly useful, mostly for attaching PDFs. I 
don't have a ton of other apps to compare it too, but it runs incredibly 
smooth, useful, works across all my devices, and I feel like I owe them 
this review after all the good this app has brought me.

text: I wish I could give this app 4.5 stars. If it integrated smoothly with Google Inbox, I would give it 5 stars for sure. It integrates very smoothly with Gmail (but I really like Inbox) so if you use Gmail, you'll love this.   You can add emails to your task list. You can say "Ok Google and a task_____" by way of an IFTTT applet, you can categorize your tasks as 'projects', and you can collaborate with others.  I bought the premium (not too expensive) and that allows me to add reminders...to my phone or via email. I use the chrome extension, though, so who needs an email when the icon is staring at you 24/7 from the top of the page! I was disappointed that I couldn't add a reminder without buying the premium, but the way the app syncs with my phone and my desktop, reminders are really not needed.   Tasks are added to my google calendar (which I toggle off, since it's so cluttered).   So far, very efficient. After I use it for another month or so, I'll re-review.

text: This app was a major disappointment. My main issue is that you can't manually change the recurrence of an event or thing to do. If you can't figure out how to phrase it correctly when you create the event, you're SOL.   I wanted to create a thing to do that occurred every 4 weeks on Sunday, but the phrasing to do so wasn't intuitive and once I figured it out, it would change it to "every Saturday" for some reason.   Also, when I assigned a parent task, it would put it under the parent and then also list it separately as it's own thing, making it look like I had twice as many things to do. Also, it kept reassigning parent tasks when I moved tasks and since there's no way to edit multiple tasks at once, I had to individually reassign the parent to each task. Overall, my experience with the app was incredibly frustrating.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Amanda, sorry to hear that. To create a task that recurs every 4 weeks starting Sunday, you just have to enter "every 4 weeks starting Sunday" or enter a specific date instead of "Sunday". Sub-tasks are visible twice only in search results where you have the option to expand a parent to check what sub-tasks it contains.

text: It's not an all in one package, but to be honest nothing exists like that yet. And maybe everyone needs something different and a complete life management system is too difficult to make for more than one person. This tool will facilitate tracking and remembering the action items you have to do on a specific day or at a specific time and also the next action items you can do during any discretionary time you might have. I still use manilla folders and a labeler for projects support files that I need to give to people in person. I'm also not satisfied with managing any project information in this app, other than simple association to know what an action is for. And I track my "someday/maybe" items, "waiting for" items, and triggers elsewhere. But when used in an already working personal productivity system that is your own, this app is the bee's knees for managing simple physical actions. So despite all the negativity I just gave it, I use this app every single day and wouldn't use anything else. It makes sense, as most of what we do everyday are just a bunch of simple actions. I've only have success when I track one action for each project. Just a tip. That's why I manage projects elsewhere. Only the very next action for each project goes in todoist, for me.

text: I have tried most of the todo apps on the market, including toodledoo, nozbe, trello, jira, asana etc.     For me, todoist is the perfect combination of structure and flexibility for my use. Very east to implement gtd systems with projects and contexts. It works great on both android and web (it seems all functionality is in both places), and the premium version is affordable enough for home use.    Very easy to create hiearchies such as subproject and different projects for work and private, while at the same time being able to create queries and views across all folders.   Possible to perform searches for just the subprojects of a given project, so you can ask for all the next actions for just work or just home.   Very easy to share projects/lists with others.  Good reminder feature.  If I have to point at anything negative, it would the lack of recursive sharing, and the fact that there is no suggestion/tab-complete when defining folter queries. Took a bit of research to find the query syntax, but was easy once I found it.

text: Probably the best to do app there is. I've been using GTasks for more than ten years. Intensively. I love its intuitive simplicity and speed. Now I need more advanced functionality and have tried a lot of different alternatives. Microsoft to do is in development and seems to aim for good stuff, but it's definitely not there yet. Dgt GTD is great. The next iteration, Soda, might be awesome, but with Todoist I found the same simplicity and intuitive interface that I loved with GTasks, a very extensive package of functionality, total flexibility of how to make my own system, and it works across all platforms, with almost identical interface. I'm impressed. I'm still in the process of digging into it's core and moving my big amount of notes into Todoist, but it's already working way better for me than any other I've seen. I'm still on the free version, which I think is plenty for most users permanently. I'll most likely move onto the paid version, since I'm a heavy user and probably can find enough value in the added functionality to make it worth the small amount of money. Spotify costs more than 4 times as much, so not much of a question....

text: After going back and forth between Todoist and TickTick for the past year (TickTick being my main ToDo app for several years), I have finally settled on Todoist. Quite simply, Todoist is the better app. It just does more. In fact, the more I really get into it the more it seems to do. This and I do prefer Todoist's UI. I like the way it looks and it just seems to flow better. It does (for the most part) everything that I need it to do...and then some. I like the ability to create projects and sub-projects within sub-projects. While TickTick does offer a Project feature (called Folders), as well as sub-projects (called Lists), they do not allow sub-projects within sub-projects.  With Todoist I can choose a different color for each individual project. This is not currently an option with TickTick. I also like the ability to create subtasks. However, I am missing the ability to create checklists within a single task, which is a TickTick feature that I used regularly. I especially like (with TickTick) that I could (within a single task) add different times for individual items on checklist. After every item was checked, the task was set to repeat, along with the checklist. I'm not sure why Todoist doesn't offer this feature but I am hoping they will add it. Still, Todoist is packed with a multitude of features, some of which I am still discovering. To get the most out out of Todoist, I do recommend visiting their website, as well as watching YouTube tutorials by seasoned Todoist users. My new favorite thing is the ability to create filters. I also like the ability to create uncompletable tasks. Not to mention, I am making serious use of the label feature. Needless to say, I'm all in. I officially love Todoist!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: LeeAnn, you can create checklists with sub-tasks. In fact, you can even create a sub-project with regular recurring tasks which would work as a checklist :) Still, we'll look into improving this in the future.

text: I LIVE, BREATHE & LOVE Todoist. Bought a year subscription after about 20 days of using it. I was an Outlook tasks user for YEARS, it was the ONLY way to manage my workload, until I found Todoist & never looked back. I've been using it for over 6 months now, I believe. 😊 Todoist is an awesome, almost flawless, near PERFECT task manager. If using Outlook, I HIGHLY, HIGHLY recommend that you download the Outlook add-in. I use the add-in daily & if I'm on the go I use the app on my phone (shortcut to add a task is AWESOME btw!). However, I hardly touch the Windows 10 app. I would love to use the Windows 10 app more, however it lacks the ability to attach emails to tasks easily. Todoist wouldn't work for me without the Outlook add-in, it's definitely an essential must-have feature.  Todoist, please incorporate some sort of implementation of Outlook &/or Office 365 into the Windows 10 app. Also, please fix the issue with subtasks (I don't understand why the parent task shows as a separate item randomly, even when I * to make it "not a task", but a title). I'd like the parent task to show, then I need to expand to see subtasks, not have subtasks listed randomly everywhere. I hope that makes sense. I guess maybe like a checklist function? I'd also like the ability to set my own default filter to filter out a certain project or label from my running to-do list.  Other than those few requests, I have NO issues with Todoist. It helps me be efficient & on top of my workload daily.  Thank you Todoist!
author: A Google user

text: I need to clarify my last review with an edit. Some functionality of the Windows 10 version of this app have gone away. The Windows 8 version worked perfectly, but when using the Windows 10 desktop version of Todoist, you can no longer search a task and then edit that task from the search results. Nor can you see or edit the reminder time once you have set it. If you have over a hundred tasks in your task list spanning 10 years as I do, this is an annoyance. Other versions of Todoist work well in these regards, including the Chrome extension and the smartphone app.  My work around it to go into the Chrome extension when I need to search and edit or check on a reminder. I wish Todoist would let you delete completed tasks.  They do not interfere with anything, and it is an intensional design feature so you don't ever loose tasks, according to the very responsive and helpful Todist support. Never the less, I find it annoying. Todoist support acknoledged the Windows 10 issue. All things considered, Todoist is still my favorite multi-platform task list program. The others multi platform task list apps don't come close. Yes, Wunderlist and Any.do, I mean you!
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Donald, after performing a search you can just click on the task's name to edit it, this hasn't changed. If a task has a reminder, all you have to do is hover over the clock icon to see all details about all its reminders. text: Here is a review after I used the app for over two years (one year free, one year paid, back to free now).  The app is great, definitely my favorite to-do app after trying out over 5 others, and having a bad time managing my time.   Free version highlights: - good minimalistic interface  - frequent updates - shortcut support  - custom natural language queries - smart re-scheduling based on AI algorithms  - priority sorting - good search for custom filters - nice karma point system for game junkies  Paid version highlights: - supports @tags - calendar syncing - custom filter support - good project support for multiple users  What I would love to have: - custom and more complex keyboard shortcuts - custom priorities + colors - more custom colors for projects (see Life Calendar colors for example, I want to have those) - have the calendar sync be a free option (just to get people in) - add some icons, like in Wunderlist - would like to have more graphs - (Web version) Add a button to move to a project when editing a task  Leaving it at 5 stars knowing the devs like to listen and we'll see updates eventually. Recommend it to any programmer,  and others.

text: Good app. A bit tricky at first, if you come from MS Outlook, for example. But once you get used to how it works, and how to program new todo's and reminders, it's very good.   For me, however, it lacks very important features. For example, let's imagine that ten notification reminders pop up in your cell phone at 8:00 a.m. For some reason, you have to restart your phone (e.g., it falls down and the battery slips off.) When you do so, your notifications are gone---and if they were a lot, you just won't remember which they were. Or, for example, let's imagine one notification pops up, and you take a look at the comment attached to it. After that, if you move to any other app or just return to home screen in your phone, notification is gone, even though you have not completed that todo.   There is no way to take a look at which todo's have notifications programmed for today (you can only see which todo's due dates are set for today.) Also it would be nice to have a way to take an easy look to a calendar when programming a reminder---currently you can only take a glimpse at a calendar when setting the due date.

text: This is the one! I've pretty much tried every task manager that's been out there but this is by far the best thing out there. Here are the highlights: APP SUPPORT:  Todoist supports EVERYTHING. I have a Mac, a PC, an android phone and an iPad and there are apps for all of them. And in the end up mostly using the web app because it's so good.  EASE OF ADDING TODOS:  You can add todos from anywhere, hotkey from any app in mac, the notifications screen in android, typing q in the web app, forwarding an email.  NATURAL LANGUAGE DATES/PROJECTS:  Todoist is even better than RTM. You can type, "Send weekly update every week on Friday #Work @office" and it will create a todo recurring every Friday in your Work list tagged with "office". Other apps force you to go to menus, drag things to the list you want and all sorts of horribleness. (I'm looking at you Wunderlist)  ADVANCED FEATURES: Too many to name. My faves: Set a time on a todo and it texts you a reminder, Space for project notes, unlimited comments on todos, photos added to todos, custom filters (Like todos for all my work projects due today).  Stop looking. Just get this.

text: Couldn't be happier.  Been using a number of Todo list apps on IOS, Android and PC for years and struggled to get one I was happy with; easy to use, seamless syncing across all my devices, nice interface and allowing me to group and arrange tasks as I wish.    Todoist has ticked the boxes.  It allows easy sorting, scheduling and grouping of tasks and basically does what it says on the tin very well.  Most importantly however it does so with a very slick interface that gets the trade-off between functionality and form just right.   The web interface is classy, as is the IOS interface.  The Android app (at least on my phone as opposed to my iPad)  is a bit more constrained but I suspect this is due to screen size limitations.  Finally, Todoist is well supported - there are maintenance updates to the web version occurring almost daily and a constant stream of new features.  So highly recommended.

If you have a dozen items in your list, you wont be able to see whats coming up without scrolling.   5) Every time you press the wrong button, you get a pop-up window telling you that it is a premium feature button. The premium buttons are  annoyingly located next to the  buttons you actually need! 6) You can't type in a date due to the apps mandated "intelligence." text: Todoist is a pretty powerful app that can go a step beyond a to-do list, and it's particularly good for people who tend to work solo -  a lot of the other popular task lists/managers are really geared toward teams, and while that's great, I don't often work as part of a regular coordinated team, so a lot of the features of those other applications really don't apply to me.  I'd say that Todoist's best feature is the clean user interface. It's easy to read, easy to add tasks to (and the Chrome extension is very good for this) and lays out what you need to do for the week very nicely.  There are some cons, though. It's not obvious how to create subtasks and there's an extra step involved that I don't think is necessary. There are a couple of snags relating to repeating tasks. If you have a repeating task with subtasks, the subtasks are not "uncompleted" when the task refreshes (only the parent task is). If you have a repeating task that is overdue and you mark it as done, the current deadline is skipped and the task refreshes for the next one, which can throw you off a bit if you still have to  do the task for the current period.  All in all, it's a worth a try.

text: Todoist is not the most aesthetically attractive of the various task list apps out there, but for the most part, it is very functional. It's easy enough to quickly add tasks in the app, but I personally prefer adding things online or through the web app because it's much faster to type than it is to keep tapping keys on my phone.  What I like most about the app is that it is easily customizable. The app doesn't have any default categories to start you with; you are free to create "projects" viewable in the side bar as you wish, or none if that's more your style. This is the case for pretty much all of the other functions: they work, but if you don't feel like using them you don't have to.   If you like keeping a task list, at the end of the day it doesn't really matter which tools (digital or non-digital) you use to do it as long as you are effectively getting things done. Todoist is a great choice, but if you don't like the layout there are plenty of other options.

text: ToDoIst falls short of the GTD mantra in one key way: the focus is on setting labels, reminders, and projects at the time of task creation, and not IN BULK. With GTD you are supposed to dump all of your ideas into an inbox, then move each idea/task into smaller chunks with labels, reminders, projects IN BULK. This is to decrease the TIME and ENERGY it takes to create a workflow. With ToDoIst you have to INDIVIDUALLY edit each task's label, reminder, and project. This is a huge waste of time when you have 20 things in your inbox that need to be quickly sorted. It's, ironically, almost the complete opposite of the GTD mantra. All in all I think TDI is fantastic, but there really needs to be a "bulk" edit option to really take it to the next level. I understand that you can do this with due dates, but that's pretty much it. This needs to be applied to labels, reminders, and projects as well. If I need to quickly label 5 tasks as "y" and 8 tasks with reminders, I should not have to edit 13 different tasks independently.

text: The reason people use apps like these are not just to remember the things they have to do, but also to keep track of their progress, and inherently get a sense of reward when their tasks are finished. Of course, a completed task should be a reward in and of itself, but the ability to see your progress is very motivating. Unfortunately, ToDoist does not allow that - completed tasks disappear from their projects and the Today view, and are only visible with all the other historical completed tasks in a separate section of the app.  Users have been asking for this feature in a thread that's over a year old, and the company does not seem to think it is a priority.   I'm a premium user, and when my subscription ends I'll be moving on. In fact, if I find an app that does this and has the features of ToDoist, I'll leave, regardless of how much of my subscription I have used.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Andy, we're very sorry to hear that. If you have tasks that you want to see on your list after completion, you can use sub-tasks which stay there until their parent task is completed. You can of course also see them on the completed task list.

text: Todoist likes to pretend to be a free app, but to suggest that the free version is anything less than a trial is downright dishonest. Some pretty fundamental features, such as task reminders, are only available to premium users. What's worse, Todoist Free doesn't highlight which features are premium until you try to use them, meaning free users are constantly thwarted by popups asking them to spend money.  Rather than simply sell you the app, Todoist asks you to pay a sizable $29/year subscription fee, which in my view is a big downside compared to other similar apps.   All that griping set aside, I have to admit that it is a quality app. It's intuitive, simple, and highly customizable. I did a lot of shopping around an this is the only productivity app that does everything I want. I'm just hoping a cheaper alternative will emerge in the near future.

text: The app has a glaring bug: the calculation for daily repeating tasks breaks if you mark a daily task as complete after midnight. Instead of calculating one day from when the task is due, it calculates from when the task is marked done making the next due date tomorrow thus skipping today -- even though this is a daily task. This is a bug the developers know about and refuse to fix.  The location feature, like a few other features in this app, is incomplete.  It neither allows for the use of common locations (Home, Work, etc.), it also doesn't use Google's own starred locations. So, every time I want a reminder for when I arrive home, I have to enter the complete address (which autofills incorrectly).  Which renders this high-touted feature completely useless in practice. The app should either allow the selection of oft-used addresses from a list or use Google-starred addresses.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hello Joey. Sorry if recurring tasks doesn't fit your workflow... this is actually a design decision based on data, where most people find it more intuitive to base it on your current time. Also, Home/Work are not accessible, so we can't use them. Finally, you should be able to pick recent locations in 1 tap. If not, please reach out to us. Thanks!

text: The app is ok and has interesting features - some may even be outstanding (like the location awareness - if it gets available on Android,  too). It is a pity, that there is no way to try many of these without buying the premium version. The UI is not very intuitive at some places. And why the Windows version has no real alert feature but insteads "alerts" you by sending "emails to self" is beyond me! ||-(  However, the biggest shortcoming which is making the app practically useless to me, is the missing sync with Outlook tasks!  The suggested way to import OL tasks into Todoist via "email-to-self" can only be called unrealistic (to state that very politely)! But also the other direction, forwarding a task's completion entered in Todoist to Outlook (and thereby possibly triggering notifications to other people) would be an absolute requirement for using Todoist in any typical office environment.  Concluding: an interesting app, but waiting for the absolutely required sync-capability with Outlook (at least in the PC version)!

text: If you just want some basic lists, ToDoist will do the job... that's where it ends. As a paid task list or to do manager. It fails on too many levels. Here are a few:  No Sorting: You cannot sort your tasks into due date order. This should be one of the most basic features of any task manager. You are required to use the 7 day view for this functionality, or the web version to order them. But as soon as you add a new task, it goes to the bottom regardless of due date.  Adding Task Dates: Adding due dates to tasks using terminology rather than the date picker is almost impossible. You need to write it in the exact format ToDoist specify, otherwise it won't work. If you want to see this functionality work well, check out Remember The Milk.  Reminders: Sometimes an automatic reminder will be set for a task, sometimes it won't. Even if it is set, it's hit or miss as to whether you will actually get it.  Sub-Tasks: You have to indent tasks to add sub-tasks. This is very unintuitive and means you'll often add sub-tasks in the wrong place.  Summary: Basically it's taken me more time to work around the ToDoist functionality than it's aided me as a task manager.

If you drag a regular task you'd expect it to behave the way a lot of apps do and drop it inside a subtask, but this doesn't work that way. Drag a task up into a subtask and it suddenly becomes the parent of that subtask and all the subtasks beneath it. How does that make any sense? When would I ever want to do that? Not to mention there's a long standing bug that when you go to edit a task and change the list it's in, it may or may not actually move. Right now I have two tasks that just live in the next 7 days view, and don't exsist in a list. text: I love the android app, the minimalistic design and all its features. I even got the Chrome app extension since I go between my tablet and laptop a lot. It wasn't long until I came across the first bugs, involving the calendar. When I create a task on my laptop for Oct 31st, on my tablet it synchs as Nov 1st. When I go to change the date on my tablet, it doesn't work. When it does, the same task on my laptop doesn't reflect the change once synchronized. It gets really frustrating really quick. Why do all tasks I create on the website get bumped a day ahead on the android app? The timezones are the same on all platforms. Also, the sorting the tasks by date seems to work whenever it wants. I would really want to use ToDoist for both the personal and professional spectrums, I even wanted to go Premium, however its reliability right now worries me into avoiding it.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Roland, we're sorry to hear that. Based on past reports and our testing, the only way to trigger such behavior is having the time zone set differently that on Todoist and other devices you use it on. Even if your clock may be correct, if the zone isn't - tasks will be 1 day ahead. Please contact https://todoist.com/Support_Android/ for details.

Being able to view tasks on the Android, iOS (haven't tried that yet), AND the web is a nice feature. I can now drag tasks from one project to another, color-code them according to priority, or type of task (something that I must do outside or several phases of the same task, for example). It's quite flexible and intuitive. It helps me avoid forgetting things, keeps me from feeling so overwhelmed by constantly thinking of things I need to or forgot to do (and because I can break things into small, manageable tasks), and I love clicking things off my to-do list. It also saves me time, because I enter labels by store or town, and then I can quickly sort them to group tasks together. It will send updates to email, but I access it on my office computer and my tablet, and it's great that I can do that both places and it's always in sync. No, nobody is paying me to write this rave review! I tried several similar apps, and this one's the best for me. And it even makes weekly productivity graphs for you! Perfect.

text: Indispensable para sacarle todo el partido a tu día.  Si le dedicas el tiempo necesario, en la primera semana puedes haber amortizado el paquete premium sólo por las horas que no has desperdiciado inúltilmente. Puedes clasificar por proyectos, prioridades y tags (especialmente últiles las de lugar y duración). Además, está el karma, que te obliga a partir las tareas en elementos cada vez más pequeños, concretos y más rápidos de completar.  Ojo, lo primero que deberías encontrar es un método que debería ser independiente de la app (GTD puede ser un buen comienzo). Luego, ajusta ese método a tus objetivos. Una vez tengas las líneas básicas de funcionamiento de tu método para tus objetivos puedes empezar a ajustarlo a la app y aquí es dónde la magia empieza a fluir y la cosas se empizan a hacer casi solas.

Cada nuevo proyecto requiere una lista de tareas general y diarias. El objetivo de esta app es totalmente diferente al objetivo de un calendar. Ambos son complementos uno del otro. text: Depuis que j'ai débarrassé mon téléphone des applications de "réseaux de désocialisation", c'est sans doute devenu, avec l'agenda and les mails l'une des top 3 de mes applications les plus utilisées et surtout que j'apprécie le plus. J'utilise une combinaison de la version web quand je travaille sur ordinateur, de la version mobile quand je me déplace et des plugin pour gmail pour créer des tâches depuis mes mails. Le tout me sert de système intégré pour appliquer la méthode de productivité GTD(Getting Things Done) de David Allen. Parmi toutes les applications et astuces que j'ai pu tester pour appliquer GTD, Todoist est la meilleure option que j'ai pu trouver. En particulier, si l'on suit les recommandation du guide GTD "Todoist setup guide" et que l'on prend un peu de temps pour réfléchir à la façon de créer des tâches dans todoist sur la base de mail (en utilisant l'option qui consiste à envoyer directement des mails au "projets" todoist), c'est vraiment une combinaison parfaite pour moi. De plus, je trouve le support très réactif, on reçoit des réponses personnalisées, dans le langue dans laquelle on a ouvert des tickets, on a pas l'impression d'un support fantôme pour lequel il faut résoudre toutes les énigme d'une escape room avant de trouver le bouton de contact et ça, quand on utiliser une app pour vraiment travailler, c'est vraiment rassurant ! Il reste quelques petits points qui pourraient encore être amélioré (et qui ne sont pas spécifiques à la version mobile) comme par exemple la possibilité de déplacer séparément les sous-tâches dans la vue tableau d'un projet ou la possibilité d'accéder à l'application ordinateur en mode offline sans avoir à se mettre d'abord online (ce qui est embêtant lorsque l'on veut travailler dans un avion par exemple). Mais dans tout cela rien de bloquant, j'adore l'application, je la recommande vivement et ça vient d'un utilisateur qui l'utilise quotidiennement depuis longtemps. (remarque afin d'éviter toute confusion, j'utilise la version pro et je travaille seul ie: sans partage de tâches ou flux de travail)
author: Morgan Bourgeois
developer_reply: Merci pour ces bons mots, Morgan ! C'est noté pour l'utilisation de l'appli offline ainsi que le déplacement des sous-tâches dans la vue tableau :)

text: Todoist est un gestionnaire de tâches INCROYABLE ! text: J'ai souscris.. +28€.  Le prix à visiblement augmenté ces derniers temps. . L'appli est bien plus ergonomique de l'application web (très compliqué de mettre des événements récurrents hors de la date du jour et impossible d'y mettre un rappel systématique - ex. Tous les 10 du mois avec rappel 2 jours avant). L'heure est très compliquée à indiquer.  L'intégration au Google Calendar est aisée mais les tâches récurrentes n'y apparaissent pas..  Je me demande même si le nombre n'est pas limité car cela n'a marché que pour quelques tâches aléatoirement. Le système de notification SMS ne fonctionne pas pour la France. Ça peut se comprendre. L'idée d'alerte suivant le lieu est intéressante, j'attends de tester tout de même, surtout les notions de "Quand j'arrive" et "Quand je pars".. Les rappels téléphoniques ne donne pas la description de la tache, il faut entrer dans l'appli. En résumé, je regrette mon achat, et je le trouve bien moins ergonomique, moins user friendly qu'Any.do. La version web est étroite.. Pourquoi ? J'ai fait une demande de remboursement (vu que je l'ai acquis hier), en attente de leur réponse.
author: Un utilisateur de Google
developer_reply: The price has always been 28,99 USD and has not increased. What changed is the exchange rate between USD and EUR. Furthermore, since 2016, we're forced to include VAT in the price for EU customers. SMS notifications do work in France. If you've contacted us with a refund request, you will definitely receive a refund soon.

text: Tried Todoist Premium for the 2nd time and finally gave up on it. You can add tasks with due dates,  but you cannot plan them by assigning them a start date. So you end up with very cumbersome workarounds to plan tasks manually yourself or make all kinds of list and priorities just to prevent you see the task for the first time on the due date popping up.  Despite user requests for this and this being the main theme in reviews, Todoist has not picked this up for a long time and they don's seem to be in  touch with the user community. Todoist is for people that have a few actions here and there, but for sure not for professional use.

text: The concept of Todoist is very nice: it is crossplatfrom and you can link tasks to Gmail and Outlook messages. However, it is not possible to filter on labels in the free Todoist app. This makes it unsuitable to use for GTD purposes. The web app is better in this respect, it allows filtering (though you cannot store your filters). I find paying $29 a year too much to get the extra features. So this otherwise nice app is not for me.
author: Een Google-gebruiker
developer_reply: Henk :) We can't offer all features for free and maintaining a high level cloud-based software with multi-platforms. We're constantly developing new and improving old services. An annual subscription with label filtration among other features costs less than $2.50/monthly! We’re sorry to see the price has influenced the rating so significantly. :´(

developer_reply:
Oi Kaio,

Obrigado!

As tarefas concluídas podem ser acessadas sempre pelo projeto onde elas foram criadas ao tocar nos três pontinhos > Mostrar tarefas concluídas.

As tarefas recorrentes são tarefas únicas com vencimento dinâmico. Isso significa que quando ela for concluída ela aparecerá no próximo dia automaticamente.

text: O aplicativo tem muitas funções avançadas de tarefas, como tags, sistema de pontuação e filtros. Todavia, o essencial que é selincronizar bem entre dispositivos multiplataformas o mesmo falha. Quando escrevo algo no computador, e vejo no aplicativo (do smartphone) já aberto ou no próprio widget, ele não sincroniza, a não ser que eu aperte no botão de sincronizar. A versão gratuita tem várias limitações, como a impossibilidade de usar tags, fazer comentários, anexar arquivos, adicionar lembretes e criação máxima de 150 tarefas por projeto. Outra grande falha é não poder ordenar as tarefas nos filtros. O To Do (da Microsoft) é totalmente gratuito, apresentando as características pagas do Todoist, e sincroniza perfeitamente.
author: Bruno Araújo
developer_reply: Hi Bruno, we really appreciate your detailed feedback! This has been noted!

text: Foram inúmeros métodos de autogerenciamento, agenda, excel, calendário, Trello, mas nada se comparou à experiência que tenho com o Todoist.  Me engajei de maneira brusca com o app, eliminando dezenas de procrastinações em poucas semanas (atualmente sou Expert no Karma :D). Hoje, organizo toda a minha vida pessoal, bem estar, educação, trabalho, financeiro pelo Todoist.  Pensei em insights que agregariam valor à experiência de usuários mais engajados (como o meu caso):  1- Possibilidade de determinar pesos para ponderar o nível de dificuldade de cada atividade (e consequentemente o karma); Por exemplo: Correr 10km teria um valor de "energia gasta" muito superior na minha concepção do que pagar a conta de luz. 2- Criação de dashboards (ou de integração com algum dashboard) de forma a acompanhar gráficos e insights de desempenho que vão além do limitado espaço de 1 semana oferecido pelo gráfico de Karma. 3- Acesso a insights sobre o rendimento atual x médias individuais ou ainda comparando com toda a população todoist (vejam o novo Guia Bolso faz).  Enfim, desci de cabeça no funil de vendas de vocês e virei um brand lover. Me avisem se um dia precisarem de um Inside Sales :)

o prpblema é nas tarefas recorrentes... Nao eh possivel apagar 1 sem apagar 
todas... Tbm tem um problema de layout (na minha opinião) quando vc vai ver 
o calendário com as tarefas elas não aparecem dentro do quadro do dia mais 
para cima ou mais pra baixo indicando se eh manha, tarde ou noite... Para 
pessoas mais visuais, como eu, isso ajuda muito
author: Um usuário do Google
developer_reply:
Olá, obrigado por nos deixar seu feedback :) Tarefas recorrentes são repetições de uma tarefa. Para pular um dia sem atrapalhar as próximas recorrências, basta adiá-la utilizando as opções de agendamento. 
Sobre o layout, poderia nos enviar uma mensagem para support@todoist.com mostrando qual calendário você está se referindo?

text:
O App é muito bom, experimentei o pago mas uso a versão free pelo preço da 
assinatura, que para o Brazil acaba sendo muito caro e eu não preciso de 
tudo isso ainda. Achei bastante inteligente, mas só na versão paga que é 
mais completo também. Acho que poderia existir um sistema de pontos e não 
de Karma que acaba parecendo algo religioso. Em todo caso da para 
desabilitar e não é algo importante no App. Importante é o App funcionar 
muito bem. Para quem pretende usar a fundo o App recomendo entrar no Blog e 
ler muito, mas muito mesmo. Pois apesar de parecer simples a versão paga 
faz muito mais que a versão free, então quem não ler não vai aprender os 
segredos do App. Recomendo muito a leitura de todas as dicas. Espero que um 
dia os preços do App fique bom para o Brazil, assim como faz o Evernote 
para nós brasileiros, porque pagar 3x mais caro por conta da nossa moeda 
desvalorizada é bastante complicado. Pagamos muitos impostos e o que sobra 
não chega a ser suficiente para termos assinaturas de tudo que precisamos e 
gostaríamos de ter. Temos que ficar migrando de serviços ou só assinar 
aquilo que realmente achamos importante e que nós dê retorno financeiro pra 
isso. Seria de uma grande ajuda termos um preço diferenciado por conta da 
nossa moeda local. No mais o App é ótimo e recomendo o uso mesmo para 
planos free.

Excelente gerenciador de tarefas, sofisticado pela sua simplicidade apesar das inúmeras ferramentas oferecidas gratuitamente. A versão gratuita atende, no meu caso, ao gerenciamento de tarefas pessoais. Só estou sentindo muita falta de duas ferramentas (e por isso as quatro estrelas):  1) uma forma de marcar as tarefas como feitas no dia anterior; e  2) a opção de marcar algumas tarefas como "muito importante" (com estrela ou algo assim) para que sempre apareça na tela inicial, seja "hoje" ou "próximos 7 dias", independente de sua data.
author: Um usuário do Google
developer_reply: Bruna, reg. point 2 - you could try to label some tasks as @important and then create a custom filter with a query such as "@important, overdue, 7 days", then set it as your start page and use it instead of the default today/7 days views :)

text: Não sincroniza direito se você tenta criar uma tarefa sem estar conectado. Às vezes ele mostra uma mensagem de erro que te dá a chance de tentar de novo (indefinitivamente, porque uma vez que ele decide que não consegue sincronizar uma tarefa ele não sincroniza nunca mais) ou mandar um e-mail pro desenvolvedor (que não vai ser entregue com sucesso). Na maior parte das vezes ele simplesmente não atualiza e você precisa se lembrar de que tem tarefas no celular que não estão aparecendo na web. Além disso, quando você cria uma tarefa nova ele gosta de não estabelecer um projeto só pra você perder tempo enquanto ele carrega sua lista.
author: Um usuário do Google

text: Pra mim é o melhor, pois permite desde lista de tarefas simples ao gerenciamento de pequenos projetos, passando pelo uso como caderno de notas, para salvar fotos, documentos digitalizados, gravações de voz, e também como agenda telefônica (salvando o nome do contato como tarefa e os telefones como notas dessa tarefa) ou  agenda de compromissos. Também é integrado com o Gmail permitindo sincronizar a agenda, transformar correios recebidos em tarefas,  como retornar à um cliente ou colocar alguma mensagem de site de compras como lembrete da sua próxima compra na sua lista de "coisas que quero comprar" ou ainda enviando um email para sua conta do todoist para criar uma tarefa rápida de forma remota....e ainda roda no celular, tablet, desktop e web, ou seja, vc nunca vai esquecer de anotar alguma tarefa futura ou algum compromisso agendado. A interface é intuitiva, permitindo, por exemplo, arrastar tarefas de um dia para o outro com os dedos no tablet e celular, alem de um layout clean. Por fim, permite também o uso da metodologia GTD. O que mais dizer? Completasso !!!! Recomendo a versão paga no pacote anual, porque o ganho de produtividade mas que compensa o pequeno valor mensal.

text: This must be a joke... The most basic and important on a task manager is the reminder, that's why you need a task manger for... to remind you! So if you want reminders to work on Todoist you have to  sign a Premium Account! So this free version is completely useless because can't remind you of the tasks....  I was considering a Premium account before I new this but after I discovered this, no way my friends theres other alternatives like EVERYDAY and WUNDERLIST. TODOIST you need to change your line of thinking! _______________________________________________________________________________ Esta aplicação deve ser uma piada..... A função mais básica e importante de um gestor de tarefas é os avisos, é por isso que se precisa de um gestor de tarefas... para o avisar! Se quiser que os avisos funcionem no TODOIST tem de subscrever uma conta Premium! Então esta versão gratuita é completamente inutil, porque não lhe consegue avisar das tarefas! Estava para subscrever uma conta Premium mas depois de me ter apercebido disto, nem pensar meus amigos, existem outras aplicações alternativas como o EVERYDAY e o WUNDERLIST. TODOIST mudem a vossa linha de pensamento!

Contudo, é ridículo não ter nenhuma notificação / push na versão gratuíta, o que, para mim, é essencial. Também percebi a ausência de classificação por data / hora, a mesma falha do Wunderlist. Tinha o Astrid que é perfeito, até a estúpida da Yahoo encerrar o serviço. Agora me contendo com o Any.do.    / The product is very good. However, it is ridiculous to have no notification / push in the free version, which, for me, is essential. I also noticed the lack of classification by date / time, the same failure Wunderlist. Astrid had that is perfect, even the stupid Yahoo terminate service. Now I containing the Any.do.
author: Um usuário do Google
developer_reply: Victor, infelizmente não podemos oferecer todas as funcionalidades gratuitamente e continuar ativos em 11 plataformas diferentes. Introduzimos novas funcionalidades e gostamos de ouvir os nossos utilizadores. Nas listas "Hoje" e "Próximos 7 dias" as suas tarefas são ordenadas por data e hora e com o Todoist Premium pode geri-las com outros filtros.
